open_items: ECB: cycle 1357's provider_down resolved by cycle 1358 and stayed healthy through cycle 1360 (monitor's own view). But a live recheck at 2026-11-15T12:43Z, about 41 minutes after cycle 1360 finished, got HTTP 503 from both the ECB dataflow and data endpoints, with ECB's own branded maintenance page ('We are experiencing some problems at the moment'), not the chronic empty-error or ReadTimeout pattern. This is a third distinct ECB failure shape (after the fixed 406-on-csv pattern and the cycle 1357 empty-error/ReadTimeout pattern) and is not yet reflected in any completed cycle. Watch cycle 1361 (expected ~14:01Z): if it also shows ECB failing, treat this as a real new outage pattern worth its own tracking, not noise.

Monitor bug noted previously: /api/history computes status without contracts, so a contract-only degraded state never shows up in /api/history, only in /api/status and /api/contracts. Not re-verified this run.

Chronic gateway bug (empty 'Error: ' message from tools/sdmx_tools.py around lines 207-209 catching Exception with an empty str(e)): previously traced on ABS (many occurrences), ESTAT (cycle 1143, 1335), and ECB (cycle 1337, 1339-adjacent, 1345, 1357). Not observed this run (cycle 1360 was fully healthy). Not fixed by this routine; it only commits to docs/monitor/.

Long-running architectural facts, not incidents: ILO /availableconstraint/ returns 500 (constraints come via ?references=all); ECB does not support /availableconstraint/ (404 is expected, not an error); ESTAT has no practical constraint support; ESTAT direct json check is skipped by design (Eurostat returns 406 for SDMx-JSON); IMF direct json check is skipped by design (IMF ignores the JSON Accept header and returns XML); STATSNZ direct json check is skipped by design (Stats NZ ignores the JSON Accept header and returns CSV); BIS/IMF/ILO references:contentconstraint reads ignored (accepted and silently dropped, seen again this run on BIS, ILO, IMF); encoding:structure_xml Content-Type charset/version parameter order flips cosmetically from time to time across ABS/FBOS/ILO/SBS/OECD, verdict stays ok as always (seen again this run on OECD).
